newsitem.title: GREECE: Athens bourse closes lower in light trade.
newsitem.headline: Athens bourse closes lower in light trade.

text.p: Greek shares ended lower in thin volume on Friday, with many investors wary of the market due to persistent settlement problems this week and strikes to protest against the 1997 austerity budget.

"The market has stabilised in the 900-930 range. If we could put the settlement problems behind, there is a chance of a rally before year-end," said Apostolos Constantinidis at Alpha Trust-Hambros Hellenic.
The general share index closed at 910.19, down 0.04 percent or 0.33 points, compared to Thursday's 910.52 finish. Turnover was 2.82 billion drachmas.
In recent days a string of brokerages has been banned from trading by bourse authorities for a single day for failing to meet a rigid settlement deadline of 48 hours.

"It's an absurd issue which the authorities should sort out quickly. Imagine what foreign investors think when we tell them we've been banned from trading for the day," said a broker at a large firm who asked not to be named.

Bourse authorities began strictly applying the settlement rule, and punishing offenders, after Delta Securities tried to pay 2.6 billion drachmas with bad cheques at the clearing house early this month. Three Delta officials were charged with fraud.
But brokers, especially those with foreign clients, have complained that the 48-hour period is too short and that they will suffered regular problems unless a solution is found.

The settlement row and a nationwide strike on Thursday to protest against the budget were keeping investors away. The main north-south road linking Athens to Salonika was still blockaded on Friday by protesting farmers.
Brokers said there were no surprises in the draft budget presented by National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou on Friday but they were concerned over possible implications of Thursday's strike.

"Following social unrest, the government revised its position however on the issue of tax exemptions to workers. Tax exemptions that apply to them will not be lifted in 1996 but in 1997," ING Barings said in its daily report.
Decliners led advancers 96 to 90 with 36 issues unchanged on 222 traded.
